newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: De Beers Orapa project to create 2,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: De Beers Orapa project to create 2,000 jobs.

text.p: The 1.3 billion rand production expansion project at Botswana's Orapa diamond mine will create 2,000 jobs during construction, Debswana Diamond Company managing director Baledzi Gaolathe said.
Debswana -- a 50-50 partnership between the Botswana government and diamond giant De Beers -- operates three mines and employs 6,000 of the country's 1.5 million population.

Orapa employs 2,682 workers and the project, announced last month, will create a further 300 long-term jobs with about 2,000 people employed during construction, which is expected to be completed by the end of the century, he told visiting reporters.
Diamond mining contributes about a third to Botswana's gross domestic product and the country relies on diamonds for about 80 percent of its foreign exchange earnings.

"Debswana is the biggest company in Botswana. The project will increase the share of diamond exports...It will increase contribution of the diamond industry to Botswana's GDP, which already accounts for one third of the total. It will create jobs and additional opportunities," Gaolathe said.

With the expansion, which will build one of the world's biggest stone processing plants, De Beers aims to more than double throughput at Orapa, lifting output to around 11.5 million carats a year by 2000 from 5.5 million in 1995.
That will lift De Beers' total Botswanan output -- mostly of gemstone quality -- by around a third to some 23 million carats.
The new plant will be fully commissioned by January 2000.
The Orapa pit currently measures 1.5 kilometres by 900 metres. After expansion, it will be 2.1 km by 1.6 km.
"All this is going ahead to ensure that Debswana's mines will remain the lowest cost producers in the world," Debswana deputy managing director Gavin Beevers said.
Debswana operates two mines in addition to Orapa.
Debswana's diamond production was 16.8 million carats in 1995 with Jwaneng contributing 10.5 million carats and Letlhakane 0.9 million.
